sources: Wikipedia, "Mising language", read 2026-11-22: Mising Agom Kébang is the primary literary body; Mising has adapted the Roman script. The article has no alphabet table. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mising_language

Partial evidence only (not an inventory): Keyman "Mising" keyboard help (SIL), read 2026-11-22, describes the "standard modified Roman script" with é (mid central vowel), í (close central unrounded vowel), ng, ny, long vowels and ’ (U+2019) as a glottal marker. https://help.keyman.com/keyboard/mising

No letters or numbers are included yet: no source we could read lists the full Mising Agom Kébang alphabet in order (Omniglot and the CIIL Mising Primer could not be read by the tooling). A Mising Agom Kébang reviewer must supply the alphabet, its order and the numerals.
